agents.what_it_does: Drafts a decision record for each case at escalation and close, covering the open questions, evidence for and against, the policy version, the decision and the reasoning, which the reviewer confirms and the team can audit later.
agents.how_it_works: A case is escalated or a decision is entered (to confirm) → the agent drafts the record from the case file: the questions raised and whether each is answered, evidence for and against, policy version and reasoning → the reviewer edits and confirms it, and the record is saved to the decision dataset with dated copies of the evidence → monthly, it flags similar cases with differing decisions for the team lead.
agents.data_it_uses: Case files, reviewer notes and decisions, policy versions in force at the time, reopened cases and the questions raised, record retention rules (all private, access to confirm).
agents.who_uses_it: Risk operations owns the record format; reviewers confirm each record; team leads use it to align reviewers on similar cases; compliance or audit reads it later.
agents.first_version: Draft records for 30 closed cases, including some that were reopened, checked by a senior reviewer for missing reasoning, missing conflicting evidence and unanswered questions.
agents.measure: Reopened cases per month; time to reconstruct a past decision for an audit request.
agents.ask_them: Where does the reasoning behind a case decision live today, and who can find it later?

problems.card: Reviewers disagree on the same kind of case
problems.statement: Similar cases receive different decisions because reviewers interpret the available evidence differently.
problems.how_it_solves: Monthly, the agent pairs similar cases that got different decisions and shows the evidence and reasoning side by side, so the lead can settle a shared rule.
problems.ask: Which type of case gets the most inconsistent decisions between reviewers?

problems.card: Case handoffs lose the reason for escalation
problems.statement: A reviewer receives an escalated case without a clear explanation of what needs investigation.
problems.how_it_solves: At escalation, the record states what needs investigating, why it was escalated and what has been ruled out, so the next reviewer starts with the open question.
problems.ask: When a case is escalated to you, what do you usually have to ask the sender?

problems.card: Case notes don't explain the final decision
problems.statement: The record says what was decided but leaves out the evidence and reasoning behind that decision.
problems.how_it_solves: The agent drafts a short reason linking the decision to the evidence and policy it relied on, and the reviewer confirms it before the case closes.
problems.ask: What does a typical closing note say today, and what would someone new need added?

problems.card: Closed cases come back with the same questions
problems.statement: A finished case is reopened because the original review did not answer the questions clearly.
problems.how_it_solves: Before closing, the agent checks the record against every question raised by the customer or the escalation and lists any left unanswered for the reviewer.
problems.ask: When a closed case reopens, what question usually brings it back?

problems.card: Case decisions are hard to audit later
problems.statement: Months after a decision, the team cannot easily reconstruct the records and reasoning used at the time.
problems.how_it_solves: Each record keeps dated copies of the evidence, the policy version in force and the reasoning, so an audit months later sees what the reviewer saw.
problems.ask: Which records change or disappear between a decision and a later audit?

problems.card: The case summary leaves out conflicting evidence
problems.statement: A summary presents one conclusion without showing the records that point to a different interpretation.
problems.how_it_solves: The record has a required section for evidence pointing the other way, which the agent fills from the case file or marks as none found.
problems.ask: When evidence conflicts on a case, where does your team record the side that lost?

agents.name: Policy-to-Checklist Sync
agents.what_it_does: Keeps each review checklist matched to the current policy, attaches the right policy version to every case, and checks each case against the checklist early, so missing records surface before final review.
agents.how_it_works: A policy document is updated → the workflow compares versions and drafts checklist edits → the policy owner approves them, and the new checklist is dated and linked to that policy version → as each case opens or moves stage (to confirm), the workflow attaches the policy and checklist that apply and lists required records still missing, well before final review; nothing blocks a case automatically.
agents.data_it_uses: Policy documents and their version history, current review checklists, case files and their stage, rules for which policy applies to which case type or region (all private, access to confirm).
agents.who_uses_it: Risk policy or compliance owns the policies and approves checklist edits; risk operations runs it; reviewers see the checklist and gaps on each case.
agents.first_version: Map one policy to its checklist, show the edits the workflow would have drafted after its last change, and run the missing-record check on 20 open cases.
agents.measure: Days from a policy change to an updated checklist; cases reaching final review with a required record missing.
agents.ask_them: How many policies govern your reviews, and how often does each one change?

problems.card: Policy updates never reach the review checklist
problems.statement: The team keeps using an old checklist after the policy governing its decisions has changed.
problems.how_it_solves: When a policy changes, the workflow compares versions and drafts the matching checklist edits, so the owner approves an updated checklist instead of remembering to write one.
problems.ask: After your last policy change, how long did the old checklist stay in use?

problems.card: Missing evidence only surfaces at final review
problems.statement: A case reaches the final reviewer before anyone notices that a required record is missing.
problems.how_it_solves: Each case is checked against its checklist at intake and at every handoff, so missing required records reach the current reviewer well before final review.
problems.ask: Which required record most often turns out to be missing at final review?

problems.card: Risk reviewers can't find the current policy
problems.statement: Reviewers spend time searching for the policy version that applies to the case in front of them.
problems.how_it_solves: Each case shows a link to the exact policy version that applies to its type, region and date, so reviewers stop searching folders for the right one.
problems.ask: Where do reviewers look for the current policy, and how do they know it's current?

agents.name: Fraud Pattern Spotter
agents.what_it_does: Looks across open and recent cases each day for shared details such as devices, addresses or payment methods, and tells the fraud lead when several cases look connected, while related cases are still open.
agents.how_it_works: Daily, the agent reads new, open and recently closed cases (to confirm) → it groups cases that share details such as a device, address, email pattern or card range, or that follow the same sequence of events → it writes a pattern note: the linked cases, what they share, what is inferred and what is still unknown → the fraud lead confirms the pattern before reviewers are alerted or any rule changes.
agents.data_it_uses: Case records and outcomes, transaction details, device, address and account identifiers, reviewer notes (all private, access to confirm).
agents.who_uses_it: The fraud lead owns it and confirms each pattern; reviewers get confirmed pattern notes on matching open cases; rule owners decide on rule changes.
agents.first_version: Run it on last quarter's cases and check whether it would have linked the patterns your team found by hand, and how many cases sooner.
agents.measure: Cases handled before a pattern was flagged, compared with past patterns; share of pattern notes the fraud lead confirms.
agents.ask_them: Thinking of the last fraud pattern you caught, which case first made someone suspicious?

problems.card: Fraud patterns are spotted one case too late
problems.statement: The team sees a recurring pattern only after several related cases have already been handled.
problems.how_it_solves: Each new case is checked against open and recent ones, so cases sharing a device or address are linked from the second case, whoever reviewed the first.
problems.ask: How do reviewers share a suspicion that a case looks like one they saw earlier?
